scope: Local reconciliation of PM-1 rows F05-01 and F05-03 (target: local validated engine) on the current branch. Evidence for a later successor scorecard; this record changes no PM-1 credit, gate or runtime state.

findings: 13 of the 16 files pinned by docs/evidence/QL_2A_BASELINE_2026-09-26.json are byte-identical at the base revision.

quant_lab/src/robot_quant/risk_evaluator.py and src/postgres/risk.js changed only in the news-window guard (missing news data no longer rejects an entry). The frozen QL-2A policy has blockDuringNews=false, so the guard is not reached.
src/postgres/ledger.js changed (Paper ledger fencing, fee reservation and exit-cost rounding) but is not imported by the QL-2A Node oracle or the Python replay closure.

verification.differentialProbe: On the retained real checkpoint market data with synthetic entry/exit flags (219 decisions), the baseline and current code produced byte-identical serial projections in Node and Python under the frozen policy; a control with the news guard enabled diverged, so the probe is sensitive.
verification.targetedSuites: Python 186 passed; Node 100 and 55 passed, 0 failed.

limits: The 92 recorded decisions and 130/130 repaint observations were not re-observed on the current code: the two TradingView chart exports used by the accepted run are not in the repository.
Some closure members (analytics.py, contracts.py, domain.js, pine-bridge readiness/registry/market) are not covered by the QL-2A implementation pins.
No evidence about current production Paper ledger cost behaviour.
Node and Python runtime versions are not pinned by the QL-2A record.
The news-guard semantics differ from the baseline for any policy with blockDuringNews=true.

F05-03.outcome: Cost, chronological validation and holdout semantics (QL-3A)
findings: Engine drift since acceptance is limited to an enqueue selection-coherence check, a two-line change in quant-research.js and the news guard; the cost replay path is byte-unchanged.
Research runs use only the v1 Paper cost model; no research path imports the v2 cost model or the PF-2 replay.
The no-overlap-with-earlier-holdout condition is a recorded Step 5 fact, not a contract rule, and is excluded from this row's contract.

verification.postgresSuites: Five existing research PostgreSQL files on a CI-like local PostgreSQL 16.15 cluster: 78 passed, 0 failed, 2 skipped in-test.

newTests.result: 22 passed, 0 failed on unmodified code (author and independent tester runs).
newTests.clauses: C1 cost model frozen from deployment evidence; C6 screens and ranking; C7 sensitivity before holdout; C9 holdout acceptance and reason codes; C10 worker report fields and completion reasons; C11 live Paper counters, positions, sessions and signals unchanged; stress and holdout evaluate exactly the selected candidate.
newTests.mutationEvidence: An independent tester applied 19 single-edit mutations to the worker, contract and enqueue code, one at a time with byte-verified restore; all 19 made at least one new test fail. Product file hashes equal the base revision afterwards.
newTests.review: Independent architecture review: acceptable with minor findings; the medium finding (finalist identity) and three low findings were fixed and re-verified.

limits: The foundation research path, the invalid-evaluation-response branch and the two in-test skipped cases are not covered by this evidence.
Historical B1-B3 runs were not replayed; their tracked evidence does not record the cost values used.
Allocations and fills tables are not seeded in the C11 check.
